extracted.intended_audience: students and readers of English poetry; literary critics and scholars of Romantic-era literature
extracted.subtask_description: Critical lecture-style standards for evaluating English Romantic poets (Scott, Wordsworth, Coleridge, Southey), emphasizing qualities such as originality, construction, poetic machinery, sentiment, and lasting influence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transformative power / determinate impression
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no determinate impression left on the mind by reading his poetry... A great mind is one that moulds the minds of others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether a poem/poet changes the reader or merely provides transient images; true greatness includes the capacity to shape other minds, not just to entertain.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entertainment versus substantive effect
rubrics_metrics.description: His poems are only entertaining. The Notes to his poems are just as entertaining as the poems themselves.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish mere entertainment value from deeper literary merit; entertaining surface qualities are insufficient to mark a work as great poetry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality / internal source of poetry
rubrics_metrics.description: Mr. Wordsworth is the most original poet now living. His poetry is not external, but internal; he furnishes it from his own mind, and is his own subject.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prize originality and poetry sprung from the poet's own mind and experience rather than reliance on tradition, borrowed stories, or impersonation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pathos and emotional beauty
rubrics_metrics.description: Many of the Lyrical Ballads... of inconceivable beauty, of perfect originality and pathos.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess presence of genuine pathos and emotional depth; individual detached pieces may display exceptional originality and feeling even if larger works falter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Constructive faculty / ability to form a whole
rubrics_metrics.description: He cannot form a whole. He has not the constructive faculty. He is totally deficient in all the machinery of poetry. The Excursion, taken as a whole... is a proof of this.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge a poet's capacity to organise large-scale works coherently — narrative progression, structural unity, and the ability to carry a reader from first line to last are essential for longer poems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Poetic machinery, meter and technical craft
rubrics_metrics.description: The line labours, the sentiment moves slow, but the poem stands stock-still... He is totally deficient in all the machinery of poetry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate mastery of technical elements (meter, cadence, form). Laboured lines, weak metrical control, or lack of formal craft diminish poetic effectiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Depth versus breadth of impression
rubrics_metrics.description: He has produced a deeper impression, and on a smaller circle, than any other of his contemporaries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider both intensity of effect (depth) and scope of influence (breadth); a poet may move a few profoundly or many superficially — both are relevant qualities to weigh.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authenticity of historical/antiquarian voice
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a modern air in the midst of the antiquarian research of Mr. Scott's poetry. It is history or tradition in masquerade.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check whether attempts at antiquarian or historical voice feel genuinely of their period or are undermined by contemporary mannerisms; anachronistic 'modern air' weakens verisimilitude.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fidelity versus mere mimicry
rubrics_metrics.description: He is to the great poet, what an excellent mimic is to a great actor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Differentiate faithful reproduction or homage from mere mimicry; a work that only imitates another's surface without adding original voice is of lesser value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Simplicity vs. affected naturalness (nature vs. art)
rubrics_metrics.description: They founded the new school on a principle of sheer humanity, on pure nature void of art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether simplicity is a genuine aesthetic choice that enhances truth and feeling or an affected rejection of necessary art and craft; 'pure nature' should not excuse lack of poetic workmanship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Novelty as sole aim (anti-pattern)
rubrics_metrics.description: Something new and original, no matter whether good, bad, or indifferent, was all that was aimed at, or considered as compatible with sound philosophy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be wary of valuing novelty alone; originality must be coupled with quality — novelty for its own sake can produce extravagance and puerility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leveling of subjects and removal of traditional figures
rubrics_metrics.description: Their poetry... levels all distinctions of nature and society; has 'no figures nor no fantasies'... it has no adventitious pride, pomp, or circumstance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider the effects of abandoning classical allusion, figures, and traditional pomp: does it reveal a new authenticity or strip the poem of necessary scope and grandeur?

rubrics_metrics.name: Openness to interdisciplinary knowledge and arts
rubrics_metrics.description: He hates all science and all art; he hates Voltaire; he hates Sir Isaac Newton... he hates music, dancing, and painting...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Value poets who engage with broader knowledge and the arts; closed disdain of other disciplines is presented as a fault that narrows poetic perspective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoidance of mechanical, disjointed, and extravagant style
rubrics_metrics.description: Of Mr. Southey's larger epics... all that I remember of them is mechanical and extravagant, heavy and superficial. His affected, disjointed style...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criticise sprawling, mechanically produced epics lacking coherent design; favour concise, well-wrought composition over quantity of indifferent matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Merit of shorter, personal compositions
rubrics_metrics.description: By far the best of his works are some of his shorter personal compositions, in which there is an ironical mixture of the quaint and serious... the Holly-tree, which is an affecting, beautiful, and modest retrospect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognise and reward compact, personal pieces that balance irony and seriousness and avoid indulgent prolixity; shorter works may better reveal a poet's genuine gifts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dramatic talent and avoidance of metaphysical jargon
rubrics_metrics.description: His tragedies... are, except a few poetical passages, drawling sentiment and metaphysical jargon. He has no genuine dramatic talent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For dramatic poetry, require coherent dramatic instinct and restraint; avoid overbearing metaphysical abstraction that hinders dramatic action and clarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Musicality and the power of voice
rubrics_metrics.description: His voice rolled on the ear like the pealing organ, and its sound alone was the music of thought.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess the musical qualities of diction and delivery — a powerful, musical voice can carry thought and feeling; sound and cadence matter greatly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Endurance / lastingness of poetic power
rubrics_metrics.description: That spell is broke; that time is gone for ever; that voice is heard no more... Though nothing can bring back the hour of glory in the grass... I do not grieve, but rather find strength in what remains behind.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge whether a poet's influence and powers endure over time or were ephemeral; lasting works leave residues of value even after their prime.
